boundary_condition: Apply this only to hotel quality ratings or customer-review thresholds; do not escalate it into a default requirement for five-star luxury, a specific destination, price level, or location type.
condition: When the synthetic user is searching for hotels and has not supplied a different rating range for the current trip.
default_action: Start by shortlisting hotels with a 4-star-or-higher hotel rating or customer-review rating above 4, rather than defaulting to lower-rated or unrated properties.
exception_condition: If the current request explicitly allows a lower range such as 3-to-4 stars, or asks to broaden because of budget or availability, include those lower-rated options for that search.
name: Four-star-level hotel quality filter
rationale: Several independent hotel dialogues request four stars or above, four stars or more, or above-four-star customer reviews. One supplied example allows 3-to-4 stars, so the coherent controlled habit is a four-star-level default that can be explicitly relaxed, not an absolute universal floor.

source_evidence.contribution: Requests a hotel star rating of four stars or more, supporting a 4-star-level quality threshold.
Requests 4 stars or above, directly supporting the default to begin with 4+ rated hotels.
Requires above-4-star customer reviews, supporting use of 4+ review quality as part of the hotel-quality default.
Gives a 3-to-4-star range, grounding the exception that lower-than-4-star options should be included only when the current request explicitly permits them.

source_examples.user_utterance: I would like for the price to be under $600 a night. I would also like it to have a hotel star rating of four stars or more. I would also like to have a hotel star rating of 4 stars.
I would like to be 4 stars or above.
I need above 4 star customer reviews.
